full_judgment:
Md. Farid Ahmed Shibli J : On the application of this Criminal Revision under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short the Code') condoning the delay of 108 days the Rule has been issued calling upon the Complainant-Opposite Party to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 8-9-2013 passed by-learned Session Judge of Narayanganj in Sessions Case No. 953 of 2013 arising out of CR Case No. 345 of 2013 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 (hereinafter termed as NI Act) should not be set-aside or this Court should not pass such other order or orders as to it may deem fit and proper. 

 Complainant-Opposite Party No. 1 (for short "the Opposite-Party") filed a com-plaint under section 138 of the NI Act alleging inter alai that the accused-petitioner (for short "the Petitioner") drew a Cheque for an amount of Taka 25 lacs against his account maintained with Sonali Bank, Dharmagonj Branch of Narayangonj to pay off clues owed to the Opposite-Party. On 24-2-2013 the Opposite-Party deposited the Cheque against his bank-account maintained with the Mercantile Bank of Narayangonj Branch for encashment, but unfortunately it was returned by the drawee-bank unpaid with a remark, "drawer's signatures differ". At one stage the Opposite-Party filed a complaint with the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate of Narayangonj after fulfilling all legal requirements of the NI Act and on receipt of the record the learned Session Judge took cognizance of the offence under section 138 of the NI Act by getting the complaint registered as Session Case No. 953 of 2013. 

 3. On 8-9-2013 the Session Case was fixed for framing of charge and hearing of the petition filed under section 265C of the Code for discharging the Petitioner. After hearing, the learned Session Judge disallowed the petition filed under section 205C and framed the charge against the petitioner under section 138 of the NI Act. Being dissatisfied with the decision and order the Petitioner has filed the instant petition under section 439 read with 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 5. Learned Advocate Mr Zaman appearing for the Petitioner alleges that the Opposite-Party had forcibly obtained the signature of the Petitioner on a blank Cheque taken out from the Cheque-Book issued in the name of Petitioner's wife Shahnaz Begum, who was the actual account-holder of the drawee-Bank i.e. the Sonali Bank and due to that reason the Cheque in question was bounced with a remark that the drawer's signature differs. Mr. Zaman contends. that when a Cheque is returned unpaid either because of insufficiency of fund or because of the fact that the Cheque amount exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made by the account holder with that Bank- only in those two cases bouncing of the Cheque will come under the mischief of section 138 of the NI Act otherwise not. Mr. Zaman further contends that as the Cheque in question has been dishonoured for difference or dissimilarity of signature of the drawer, in this case any such allegation of bouncing of the Cheque will not fall in garb of an offence punishable under section 138 of the Act. 

 6. In reply Mr. Taimur Alam Khondaker retorts contending that the above submission, as made on behalf of the Petitioner, is not sustainable in law and on the basis of such a defence case story the Petitioner cannot be absolved form the charge under section 138 of the NI Act or from facing trial thereunder. Referring to the case of Arif-uz-Zaman vs the State reported in 2013 (XXI) BLT (AD) 234, Mr. Khondaker argues that whether a Cheque was dishonoured for insufficiency of fund or dis-similarity of signature of the drawer is a question of fact, which is to be thrashed out during trial and such a question cannot be decided by the High Court Division exercising its revisional jurisdiction. According to the learned Advocate, the Trial Court has rightly framed the charge against the Petitioner under section 138 of the Act disallowing the prayer filed under section 265C of the Code and there was no error or illegality whatsoever as alleged in passing the impugned order. 

 7. In case of an offence under section 138 of the Act, the essential facts to be proved are-i) drawing of a Cheque, ii)presentation of the Cheque, iii) return of the Cheque unpaid by the drawee bank, iv) notice in writing to the drawer demanding payment and v) failure of the drawer to make payment within the prescribed period. During the hearing of this case, Mr. Zaman has tried to castigate the very propriety of the impugned order mainly on 2 grounds: firstly- the Cheque was dishonoured for dissimilarity of the Petitioner's signature and secondly- the bank account, against which the Cheque was drawn, actually belonged to the Petitioner's wife not to the Petitioner; and that is why he cannot be held liable for bouncing of the Cheque or for any offence under section 138 of the NI Act. 

 12. It is noted that the question raised in this case has already been concluded by a decision of the Appellate Division reported in 2013 (XXI) BLT (AD) 234, the relevant passage of which is extracted hereinbefore. So, Mr. Zaman, the learned Advocate for Petitioner finds it difficult to disagree with the view as expressed above. 

 13. Regard being had to what we have discussed above and attending facts and circumstances to the case, we are, therefore, inclined to hold that there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order dated 8-9-2013 passed by the learned Session Judge of Narayangonj in Sessions Case No. 953 of 2013 and that is why the instant Petition for Revision must fail. Consequently, the Rule stands discharged and the order of stay, as granted earlier by this Court, is hereby vacated.
